annotationRationale: The digit-sum divisibility test gives three valid tens digits for every allowed outer-digit pair. The multiplication principle counts the unique triples, while parity restricts the units digit.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official solution, grouping allowed tens digits by remainder modulo 3 and multiplying the numbers of choices.

review.mathCheck: There are eight allowed hundreds digits and four allowed odd units digits. The nine allowed tens digits contain exactly three representatives of each residue modulo 3, so every outer-digit pair admits three tens digits. Unique digit triples give 8·4·3=96, choice A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the first official solution 15 on page 9. The residue groups, divisibility criterion, and multiplication count agree; inclusion-exclusion is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: The two assessed nodes capture the counting method and divisibility test. Parity is correctly supporting knowledge.
